facts.text: Human factors studies how people perceive, decide and act when working with machines, and designs machines so that real people can use them safely even when tired, busy or distracted.
facts.quote: Human factors is the field that studies how people perceive, decide and act when working with machines, and designs the machine so that real people, tired or busy or distracted, can use it safely.

facts.text: A system can fail despite a perfect sensor if the operator does not notice, understand or trust the warning, or has learned to work around the warning.
facts.quote: A sensor can be perfect and the system can still fail if the operator does not notice the warning, does not understand it, does not trust it, or has learned to work around it.

facts.text: The booklet's human-factors evidence is thin where the evidence is most needed.
facts.quote: The booklet's human-factors evidence is thin where it most needs to be thick.

facts.text: The strongest off-road human-factors study used a haul-truck simulator and found that a richer proximity display reduced collision risk and braking force.
facts.quote: The strongest off-road study placed drivers in a haul-truck simulator and showed that a richer proximity display reduced collision risk and braking force

facts.text: The benefits of a richer proximity display in the haul-truck simulator study were smaller for less experienced drivers, warning against assuming one generic operator.
facts.quote: the effect was smaller with less experienced drivers, a warning against assuming one generic operator [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Industry guidance warns that human performance can change both positively and negatively after technology is introduced.
facts.quote: Industry guidance notes that "Human Performance can change both positively and negatively after technology is introduced" [Chapter 1].

facts.text: No validated model of an off-road operator exists.
facts.quote: No validated model of an off-road operator exists [Chapter 4].

facts.text: The validation plan should keep sensor uncertainty, operator-response uncertainty and machine-response uncertainty separate.
facts.quote: The booklet therefore asks the plan to keep three uncertainties separate: sensor uncertainty, operator-response uncertainty and machine-response uncertainty [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Human factors needs a separate evidence-allocation question: whether the complete intervention improves rather than degrades real operations. The proposed evidence comes from operator simulation, nuisance-intervention testing, shadow operation and staged deployment.
facts.quote: does the complete intervention improve rather than degrade real operations, answered by operator simulation, nuisance-intervention testing, shadow operation and staged deployment [Chapter 1].

facts.text: A vehicle-and-environment simulator does not represent operator adaptation, over-reliance, override behavior or mode confusion.
facts.quote: A vehicle-and-environment simulator does not represent adaptation, over-reliance, override behavior or mode confusion

facts.text: Human-in-the-loop evidence may be required for any safety claim that depends on operator actions because vehicle-and-environment simulation does not represent adaptation, over-reliance, override behavior or mode confusion.
facts.quote: human-in-the-loop evidence may be required for any safety claim that depends on what the operator does [Chapter 10].
